issue.title: Route all artifact marker writes through an atomic-replace helper, then add the directory-mtime gate to index revalidation
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-k3.6 (land phase of epic sase-k3, ACE startup critical path); named as follow-up 2 in plans:202608/ace_startup_critical_path.md.

Epic sase-k3 phase sase-k3.4 gave ACE's Tier-1 artifact-index query a 'cached' freshness policy so startup and auto-refresh skip hidden-row repair and per-row marker revalidation, and left one coalesced revalidating reconcile running after first paint on a long cadence. That reconcile still recomputes MarkerSignatures for every row: ~13 syscalls per artifact directory (8 marker stats, one read_dir, plus a stat per prompt_step_*.json).

Research report __b proposed gating each row on a single directory mtime, turning that into 1 syscall per row. The sase-k3 plan measured that gate to be UNSOUND at HEAD and deliberately did not land it: an in-place open(path, "w") rewrite of an existing marker does not move the parent directory's mtime, and SASE has such writers.

Confirmed at master 1f388edee:
- src/sase/axe/runner_artifacts.py:276 — write_done_marker writes done.json through a plain open(done_path, "w").
- src/sase/axe/run_agent_helpers_artifacts.py — read-modify-write helpers update agent_meta.json in place.
- Atomic helpers already exist to model on, e.g. src/sase/axe/agent_meta.py:16 write_agent_meta_atomic.

The plan re-counted against the live tree: 1,535 of 6,740 artifact directories (22.8%) already hold a marker newer than their own directory — 1,501 agent_meta.json, 51 done.json, 31 prompt_step_*.json, 30 workflow_state.json, 1 waiting.json. So the gate would silently skip revalidating nearly a quarter of the tree today.

Scope:
1. Route every artifact marker write (done.json, agent_meta.json, workflow_state.json, waiting.json, prompt_step_*.json) through an atomic write-temp-then-os.replace helper, so a marker mutation always moves its parent directory's mtime.
2. Only then add the directory-mtime gate to the revalidating path in sase-core (crates/sase_core, agent_scan/index.rs refresh_stale_rows / select_records), turning the background reconcile from ~4,700 x ~13 syscalls into ~4,700 x 1.

MANDATORY test, called out explicitly by the proposing plan: rewriting an existing marker in place must still trigger repair. That is the assertion that would have caught the unsoundness, and it must ship with the gate.

Work in sase-core through /sase_repo (sase repo open sase-core) and read that repo's AGENTS.md first: release-plz owns versions, do not hand-edit Cargo.toml versions or the sase-core-rs pin in pyproject.toml, and verify with sase-core's own 'just check'.

payload.entry: Triage sweep 2026-08-14 (requested by the project owner: keep the seven highest-impact open tasks, close the rest). These are all sase-k3 land-phase follow-ups on a path the epic already fixed -- first paint no longer pays persisted diff-badge classification, hidden-row repair, or the double ProjectSpec parse. What is left here is refinement (import-graph diet, marker atomic-replace + mtime gate, persisting badge classification, cold-cache re-measurement, attributing the loader 'disk' stage), none of it a correctness defect and none with an independent reporter. The one member of this group kept open is sase-kh: hidden index rows are the growth mechanism that makes ACE startup worse every week, and the live store is now 107 MB. Re-file with a +1 and a fresh measurement if any of these becomes the dominant startup cost again.

payload.close_reason: Deprioritized in the 2026-08-14 task-backlog triage: epic sase-k3 already took the ACE first-paint win these follow-ups refine.
